newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt Airport says reports record 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt Airport says reports record 1996 profit.

text.p: Frankfurt Airport AG said on Friday it expected a record 40 million passengers to pass through Germany's largest airport and to report a profit near the record level seen for 1996.
The state-owned airport set a record in 1996 with 38.77 million passengers flowing through the airport, the second-busiest in Europe behind London's Heathrow Airport.
Frankfurt Airport said it reported a record 1996 net profit of 84.2 million marks, up from 44.2 million marks in 1995, despite a two percent rise in revenues to 2.36 billion marks.
The profit gains are to come from cost-saving measures but without job cuts at the airport that serves Germany's financial centre.
The airport also said it expected to handle a record 1.4 million tonnes of freight during 1997 after setting a record in 1996 with 1.366 million tonnes.
The Bonn government owns 26 percent of Frankfurt Airport, while the state of Hesse holds 45 percent and the city of Frankfurt has a 29 percent stake.
Bonn said in June it has no plans to speed up privatisation of its airport shareholdings to ease government finances as Germany struggles to qualify for European monetary union.
Under a 1994 air transport strategy, Germany plans to dispose of its 26 percent stakes in airports in Berlin, Frankfurt, Hamburg and Munich and of a 31 percent stake in Cologne/Bonn airport.
